prerequisites: Students should master basic programming knowledge from the first semester, especially variables, control structures, functions, and simple data structures like arrays.
A basic understanding of mathematical concepts such as sets, simple logic, sums, and growth rates is also important, as these are needed for algorithm analysis.
Initial experience with systematic problem-solving and structured development of small programs is helpful.
Familiarity with development environments and a willingness to think abstractly and analytically support a successful start to the module.

learning_outcomes.text: Students gain a comprehensive overview of the fundamentals of algorithms and data structures. This includes understanding the concept of an algorithm itself, the importance of efficiency and complexity in algorithm analysis, and an overview of elementary data structures such as lists, sets, trees, and hash tables.

Students know important algorithms and data structures as well as techniques for analyzing their complexity. They can distinguish algorithms based on their quality and select, explain, and implement suitable algorithms and data structures for solving simple applications within the application context.

Students focus on a deep understanding of the properties, analysis, and application of algorithms and data structures, as well as their interaction. They learn how search and sorting algorithms work and engage with methods of algorithm design and selected algorithms on graphs.

Students reflect on and evaluate the epistemic validity of expert statements in the field of algorithms and data structures in a situation-specific manner. They are able to apply thesekenntnisse in the context of real and complex problems, critically question them, and weigh them against each other. Through this profound understanding, they can develop innovative solutions based on plausible expert considerations, thus contributing to the solution of practical and theoretical problems in computer science and related disciplines.

The practical application of acquired knowledge is paramount. Students should be able to use algorithms and data structures to solve real-world problems. This includes the ability to select appropriate data structures for specific applications and to design and implement algorithms accordingly.

Another goal is the development of communication and cooperation skills. Students learn to effectively communicate their ideas and solutions within the team. They work together to solve complex problems and learn from each other.

Students gain awareness of the ethical and societal implications of computer science. They reflect on the responsibility associated with the development and application of algorithms, particularly regarding data protection, fairness, and transparency.

syllabus_topics: Elementary Data Structures (including lists, sets, trees, hashing)

assessment_methods.method: Written exam or multiple-choice exam or written exam and multiple-choice exam

assessment_rules: The graded assessment can be a written exam, a multiple-choice exam, or a combination of both. The duration and scope of the graded assessment are defined by the current study regulations. In addition, there is an ungraded assessment consisting of experimental work (approx. 3 experiments) or practical work samples (approx. 3 assignments).
